work: Enarratio in Epistolam B. Pauli ad Titum
source: Dionysii Cartusiani Opera Omnia, t. XIII (Montreuil)

2.title: EXPOSITIO CAPITULI SECUNDI : TU AUTEM LOQUERE QUÆ DECENT.
2.title_en: Exposition of the second chapter: But speak thou the things that become sound doctrine.

paras.t: Postquam Apostolus Titum edocuit circa ordinationem episcoporum seu presbyterorum, jam instruit eum circa diligentem gubernationem subditorum suorum.
paras.en: After the Apostle has taught Titus concerning the ordination of bishops or priests, he now instructs him concerning the diligent government of his subjects.

paras.t: Tu autem, id est illis ita errantibus, tu, a[…] doctrinam […] aliorum antistes ac prædicator, […] legem quam prædicas. Nec aliquid dicas quod veræ doctrinæ non consonet.
paras.en: [[2:1|But speak thou|Tu autem]], that is, while they go so astray, thou, a[…] [[2:1|doctrine|doctrinam]] […] the overseer and preacher of others, […] the law which thou preachest. Nor shouldst thou say anything that does not agree with true doctrine.

paras.t: Senes hortare ut sobrii sint, pudici, prudentes, sani in fide, in dilectione Dei et proximi, in patientia. Hæc est salutaris doctrina.
paras.en: Exhort them: [[2:2|That the aged men be sober, chaste, prudent, sound in faith, in love|Senes hortare ut sobrii sint, pudici, prudentes, sani in fide, in dilectione]] of God and of neighbour, [[2:2|in patience|in patientia]]. This is wholesome doctrine.

paras.t: Anus similiter hortare esse in habitu sancto, id est vestibus religiosis, non criminatrices, id est aliorum accusatrices, præsertim adolescentularum, quibus ex levi suspicione crimina imponere consueverunt, non multo vino servientes, ne sint gulosæ ac vinolentæ, bene docentes suam familiam, ut prudentiam doceant, id est veram utilemque doctrinam, non incantationes vel sortilegia. Non tamen debent viros docere publice in ecclesia, quia docere hoc modo mulieri non permitto.
paras.en: Exhort [[2:3|The aged women, in like manner|Anus similiter]] to be [[2:3|in holy attire|in habitu sancto]], that is, in religious garments; [[2:3|not false accusers|non criminatrices]], that is, accusers of others, especially of young women, on whom they are wont to lay charges on slight suspicion; [[2:3|not given to much wine|non multo vino servientes]], that they be not gluttonous and given to drink; [[2:3|teaching well|bene docentes]] their household, [[2:4|That they may teach|ut prudentiam doceant]] wisdom, that is, true and profitable doctrine, not incantations or sorceries. Yet they must not teach men publicly in the church[[1 Cor 14:34||]], for [[1 Tim 2:12|I suffer not a woman to teach|docere hoc modo mulieri non permitto]] in this way.

paras.t: Adolescentulas maritatas admonere ut viros suos ament sincero affectu, non solum carnali aut naturali, ne alium quemquam respiciant, filios suos diligant naturali et spirituali amore, quærendo eis bona honesta magis quam delectabilia sive utilia. Diligere namque est alicui bonum velle. Hortare etiam eas esse prudentes, ne sicut luna et stultus, mutentur et fluctuent, castas, ne se prorsus exponant libidini, ut cum pudore debitum viris reddant magis quam exigant, sobrias, domus curam habentes, id est propriæ familiæ sollicite providentes, benignas, id est misericordes, subditas viris suis. Mulier namque si primatum habeat, contraria est viro suo. — Omnia ista a senibus, et anibus seu vetulis, et adolescentulis observanda sunt, ut non blasphemetur verbum Dei, id est, ne propter vitiosam eorum conversationem Christus vel ejus doctrina, ab infidelibus et perversis perfidisque adolescentularum maritis blasphemiam patiatur.
paras.en: They are to admonish [[2:4|the young women|Adolescentulas]] who are married [[2:4|to love their husbands|ut viros suos ament]] with sincere affection, not only carnal or natural, so that they look to no other man; [[2:4|to love their children|filios suos diligant]] with natural and spiritual love, seeking for them goods that are honest rather than pleasant or useful [these are the three kinds of good of the schools: the honest or morally good, the pleasant, and the useful]. For to love is to will good to someone. Exhort them also to be [[2:5|discreet|prudentes]], lest like the moon and the fool they change[[Ecclus 27:12||]] and waver; [[2:5|chaste|castas]], lest they give themselves up wholly to lust, so that they render the debt to their husbands with modesty rather than exact it; [[2:5|sober, having a care of the house|sobrias, domus curam habentes]], that is, providing carefully for their own household; [[2:5|gentle|benignas]], that is, merciful; [[2:5|obedient to their husbands|subditas viris suis]]. For [[Ecclus 25:30|A woman, if she have superiority, is contrary to her husband|Mulier namque si primatum habeat, contraria est viro suo]]. — All these things are to be observed by the aged men, the aged women or old women, and the young women, [[2:5|that the word of God be not blasphemed|ut non blasphemetur verbum Dei]], that is, lest because of their sinful way of life Christ or His doctrine suffer blasphemy from unbelievers and from the perverse and faithless husbands of the young women.

paras.t: Juvenes similiter hortare ut sobrii sint: quod eis potissimum necessarium est, eo quod propter calorem et multum humorem naturæ, ad vitium incontinentiæ sint proclives.
paras.en: [[2:6|Young men, in like manner, exhort that they be sober.|Juvenes similiter hortare ut sobrii sint]]: which is most of all necessary for them, since because of the heat and abundant moisture of their nature they are prone to the vice of incontinence.

paras.t: Et quia exhortatio sine virtuosa conversatione, inefficax est atque despecta, idcirco Apostolus admonet Titum. In omnibus ad salutem pertinentibus et in cunctis quæ doces, te ipsum præbe exemplum bonorum operum, copiosius agendo quæ doces. Nec solum in opere exteriori præbeas te in exemplum fidelium, sed et in doctrina, id est vera sermocinando, in integritate mentis et corporis, fideliter et continenter vivendo, in gravitate, id est probitate morum, ne sis levis aut dissolutus.
paras.en: And because exhortation without a virtuous life is ineffectual and despised, the Apostle therefore admonishes Titus: [[2:7|In all things|In omnibus]] that pertain to salvation and in everything thou teachest, [[2:7|shew thyself an example of good works|te ipsum præbe exemplum bonorum operum]], doing more abundantly the things thou teachest. And not only in outward work shouldst thou give thyself as an example to the faithful, but also [[2:7|in doctrine|in doctrina]], that is, by speaking what is true; [[2:7|in integrity|in integritate]] of mind and body, by living faithfully and continently; [[2:7|in gravity|in gravitate]], that is, uprightness of conduct, so that thou be not light or dissolute.

paras.t: Verbum tuum sit sanum, id est verum et sine læsione peccati, ut non delinquas in lingua tua, et irreprehensibile: ut is qui ex adverso est, id est adversarius noster videns apertam sanctitatem nostræ conversationis, vereatur, id est, timeat nobis resistere, nihil habens malum dicere de nobis, id est non inveniens culpam quam nobis objiciat. Unde Petrus: Hæc est, inquit, voluntas Dei, ut benefacientes, obmutescere facere imprudentium hominum ignorantiam.
paras.en: Let thy [[2:8|sound word|Verbum tuum sit sanum]] be such, that is, true and without the hurt of sin, so that thou sin not with thy tongue[[Ps 38:2||]], and one [[2:8|that can not be blamed|irreprehensibile]]: [[2:8|that he who is on the contrary part|ut is qui ex adverso est]], that is, our adversary, seeing the open holiness of our way of life, [[2:8|may be afraid|vereatur]], that is, may fear to resist us, [[2:8|having no evil to say of us|nihil habens malum dicere de nobis]], that is, finding no fault to lay against us. Hence Peter: [[1 Pet 2:15|For so is the will of God|Hæc est, inquit, voluntas Dei]], he says, [[1 Pet 2:15|that by doing well you may put to silence the ignorance of foolish men|ut benefacientes, obmutescere facere imprudentium hominum ignorantiam]].

paras.t: Servos hortare dominis suis temporalibus, etiam dyscolis, subditos esse, in omnibus licitis placentes eisdem, non contradicentes verbis dominorum suorum, non fraudantes, id est aliquid de rebus dominorum subtrahentes, nec minus debito eis servientes, sed in omnibus suis obsequiis fidem bonam, id est veram fidelitatem, ostendentes, ut doctrinam Salvatoris nostri Dei ornent, id est, commendabilem faciant, sanctam ostendant atque decorent, in omnibus operibus suis.
paras.en: [[2:9|Exhort servants|Servos hortare]] [[2:9|to be obedient to their masters|dominis suis subditos esse]] (their temporal masters, even the froward[[1 Pet 2:18||]]), [[2:9|in all things pleasing|in omnibus licitis placentes]] them in all lawful things, [[2:9|not gainsaying|non contradicentes]] the words of their masters; [[2:10|Not defrauding|non fraudantes]], that is, not withdrawing anything from their masters' goods, nor serving them less than is due; [[2:10|but in all things|sed in omnibus]] their services [[2:10|shewing good fidelity|fidem bonam]], that is, true faithfulness, [[2:10|that they may adorn the doctrine of God our Saviour|ut doctrinam Salvatoris nostri Dei ornent]], that is, make it commendable, show it holy and grace it, in all their works.

paras.t: Sic igitur alios exhortari, et te ipsum regere debes: Apparuit enim gratia, id est misericordia et pia largitio et gratiosa instructio, Dei Salvatoris nostri, id est Christi qui est salvator et Deus noster, omnibus hominibus, id est omnibus generibus hominum et ad omnium utilitatem. Sic autem apparuit in carne pro nobis a Verbo assumpta, quia per assumptam humanitatem manifestata et data est hominibus gratia Salvatoris, et ipse Christus proprio ore nos docuit, Spiritum Sanctum Apostolis insufflavit, suamque gratiam hominibus evidenter exhibuit.
paras.en: Thus, then, oughtest thou to exhort others and to rule thyself: [[2:11|For the grace|Apparuit enim gratia]], that is, the mercy and loving bounty and gracious instruction, [[2:11|of God our Saviour|Dei Salvatoris nostri]], that is, of Christ, who is our Saviour and God, [[2:11|hath appeared to all men|omnibus hominibus]], that is, to all kinds of men and for the profit of all. And it appeared thus in the flesh taken for us by the Word: for through the humanity He assumed the grace of the Saviour was made manifest and given to men, and Christ Himself taught us with His own mouth, breathed the Holy Ghost upon the Apostles[[John 20:22||]], and plainly showed forth His grace to men.

paras.t: Apparuit ergo hæc gratia et doctrina Christi, erudiens nos, ut abnegantes, id est detestantes et fugientes, impietatem, id est peccata contra Deum, ut sunt idololatria, blasphemia, et sæcularia desideria, id est inclinationes inordinatas tendentes ad bona hujus sæculi, scilicet ad divitias, honores, delicias, dominationes, etc., sobrie et juste et pie vivamus in hoc sæculo, exspectantes longanimiter ac fiducialiter beatam spem, id est felicem remunerationem speratam, videlicet gloriam sempiternam, et adventum gloriæ, id est gloriosum adventum seu manifestationem excellentiæ, magni Dei, cujus magnitudinis non est finis, et, pro id est, Salvatoris nostri Jesu Christi: cujus primus adventus fuit in humilitate, ut judicaretur; secundus erit in potestate et gloria, ut judicet. Cujus adventum præstolamur, quatenus in die judicii suscitemur, et corpus glorificatum sortiamur.
paras.en: This grace and doctrine of Christ appeared, then, [[2:12|Instructing us, that, denying|erudiens nos, ut abnegantes]], that is, detesting and fleeing, [[2:12|ungodliness|impietatem]], that is, sins against God, such as idolatry and blasphemy, [[2:12|and worldly desires|et sæcularia desideria]], that is, disordered inclinations tending to the goods of this world, namely to riches, honours, pleasures, lordships, etc., [[2:12|we should live soberly and justly and godly in this world|sobrie et juste et pie vivamus in hoc sæculo]], [[2:13|Looking for|exspectantes]] with long patience and confidence [[2:13|the blessed hope|beatam spem]], that is, the happy reward hoped for, namely everlasting glory, [[2:13|and coming of the glory|et adventum gloriæ]], that is, the glorious coming or manifestation of the excellence, [[2:13|of the great God|magni Dei]], [[Ps 144:3|of his greatness there is no end|cujus magnitudinis non est finis]], [[2:13|and our Saviour Jesus Christ|et Salvatoris nostri Jesu Christi]] (*and* standing for *that is*): whose first coming was in humility, to be judged; the second will be in power and glory, to judge. His coming we await, that on the day of judgement we may be raised up and receive a glorified body.

paras.t: Qui Christus dedit, id est, gratis, sponte et caritative obtulit, semetipsum pro nobis in ara crucis, factus obediens Patri usque ad mortem. Oblatus est enim quia ipse voluit. Unde apud Joannem loquitur: Ego sum pastor bonus, et animam meam pono pro ovibus meis. Ut nos redimeret sua pretiosissima passione ab omni iniquitate originali et actuali sive personali, et mundaret, id est, mundum efficeret, sibi, id est ad gloriam suam, populum fidelem, quem in Baptismo purgat ab omni peccato, acceptabilem, id est sibi placentem et gratum, sectatorem bonorum operum, id est bona opera jugiter sequentem seu operantem: hoc est, ideo Christus nos redemit, ut mundaret nos in Baptismo, quatenus simus ei populus acceptabilis, sectator justitiæ, etc.
paras.en: [[2:14|Who|Qui]], Christ, [[2:14|gave|dedit]], that is, freely, of His own will and out of charity offered, [[2:14|himself for us|semetipsum pro nobis]] on the altar of the cross, becoming obedient to the Father unto death. For [[Is 53:7|He was offered because it was his own will|Oblatus est enim quia ipse voluit]]. Hence He says in John: [[John 10:14|I am the good shepherd|Ego sum pastor bonus]], and [[John 10:15|I lay down my life for my sheep|animam meam pono pro ovibus meis]]. [[2:14|that he might redeem us|Ut nos redimeret]] by His most precious passion [[2:14|from all iniquity|ab omni iniquitate]], original and actual or personal, [[2:14|and might cleanse|et mundaret]], that is, make clean, [[2:14|to himself|sibi]], that is, for His own glory, [[2:14|a people|populum]] of the faithful, whom He purges from all sin in Baptism, [[2:14|acceptable|acceptabilem]], that is, pleasing and agreeable to Him, [[2:14|a pursuer of good works|sectatorem bonorum operum]], that is, one that follows or works good works continually: that is, Christ redeemed us so that He might cleanse us in Baptism[[Tit 3:5||]], that we may be to Him an acceptable people, a pursuer of justice, etc.

paras.t: Hæc quæ dixi de modo informandi et gratia Christi, loquere, id est, populo prædica, et exhortare eum ut informationi acquiescat, et Christi beneficiis gratus sit; et argue negligentes cum omni imperio, id est in virtute obedientiæ et pontificali auctoritate. Hoc dicit Apostolus, quoniam Titus plus quam populo suo expediebat, mollis fuit atque remissus, secundum Glossam. Nemo te contemnat, quasi nobilior, sapientior, senior, aut alio modo excellentior quam tu. Christi enim vicarius es, ideo amore et vice Christi es honorandus, præsertim quum Christus dixerit: Qui vos spernit, me spernit.
paras.en: [[2:15|These things|Hæc]] which I have said about the manner of instructing and about the grace of Christ, [[2:15|speak|loquere]], that is, preach to the people, [[2:15|and exhort|et exhortare]] them to accept the instruction and to be grateful for the benefits of Christ; [[2:15|and rebuke|et argue]] the negligent [[2:15|with all authority|cum omni imperio]], that is, in virtue of obedience and with pontifical authority. The Apostle says this because Titus was softer and more lax than was good for his people, according to the Gloss. [[2:15|Let no man despise thee|Nemo te contemnat]], as though he were nobler, wiser, older, or in some other way more excellent than thou. For thou art the vicar of Christ, and therefore art to be honoured for love of Christ and in His stead, especially since Christ said: [[Luke 10:16|he that despiseth you despiseth me|qui vos spernit, me spernit]].

3.title: EXPLANATIO CAPITULI TERTII : ADMONE ILLOS.
3.title_en: Explanation of the third chapter: Admonish them.

paras.t: Admone illos, id est Cretenses tibi subjectos, principibus et potestatibus subditos esse, id est spiritualibus et temporalibus dominis, seu majoribus atque minoribus præsidentibus obedire. Qui enim potestati resistit, Dei ordinationi resistit; et qui resistunt, damnationem sibi acquirunt. Dicto, id est sermoni superiorum, obedire; sed etiam ad omne opus bonum, id est a superioribus jussum, paratos esse. In hoc […] Iis enim obediendum non est.
paras.en: [[3:1|Admonish them|Admone illos]], that is, the Cretans subject to thee, [[3:1|to be subject to princes and powers|principibus et potestatibus subditos esse]], that is, to obey their spiritual and temporal lords, or those set over them, greater and lesser. For [[Rom 13:2|he that resisteth the power resisteth the ordinance of God. And they that resist purchase to themselves damnation|Qui enim potestati resistit, Dei ordinationi resistit; et qui resistunt, damnationem sibi acquirunt]]. [[3:1|To obey at a word|Dicto]], that is, at the word of superiors; and also [[3:1|to every good work|ad omne opus bonum]], that is, one commanded by superiors, [[3:1|to be ready|paratos esse]]. In this […] [some words are lost here at the end of a column]. For such are not to be obeyed.

paras.t: […] blasphemare propter adversa ab ipso irrogata: non litigiosos esse, sed modestos, id est discretos et moderatos, ostendentes omnem mansuetudinem, id est mititer se habentes, ad omnes homines.
paras.en: […] [the opening words of verse 2, *neminem*, "no man", are lost with the end of the preceding passage] [[3:2|To speak evil|blasphemare]] on account of adversities inflicted by him; [[3:2|not to be litigious but gentle|non litigiosos esse, sed modestos]], that is, discreet and moderate, [[3:2|shewing all mildness|ostendentes omnem mansuetudinem]], that is, bearing themselves mildly, [[3:2|towards all men|ad omnes homines]].

paras.t: Fuimus enim et nos aliquando, dum non credebamus in Christum, insipientes, id est sine notitia divinorum salubri, et servientes per devia vitiorum et voluptatum, sicut ovis quæ periit. Unde scriptum est: Omnes nos quasi oves erravimus; unusquisque in viam suam declinavit. Servientes, id est per modum servorum consentientes, desideriis et voluptatibus variis, id est carnalibus ac spiritualibus concupiscentiis atque deliciis; in malitia et invidia agentes, id est malitiose et invide operantes; odibiles Deo et Sanctis quantum ad esse culpæ: juxta illud Sapientiæ, Odio sunt Deo impii et impietas ejus; et in Psalmo, Odisti omnes qui operantur iniquitatem; odientes invicem.
paras.en: [[3:3|For we ourselves also were some time|Fuimus enim et nos aliquando]], while we did not believe in Christ, [[3:3|unwise|insipientes]], that is, without saving knowledge of divine things, [[3:3|erring|et servientes]] [the print reads *servientes*, "serving"; the sense and the verse call for *errantes*, "erring"] through the byways of vices and pleasures, like a sheep that is lost. Whence it is written: [[Is 53:6|All we like sheep have gone astray, every one hath turned aside into his own way|Omnes nos quasi oves erravimus; unusquisque in viam suam declinavit]]. [[3:3|Slaves|Servientes]], that is, consenting after the manner of slaves, [[3:3|to divers desires and pleasures|desideriis et voluptatibus variis]], that is, to carnal and spiritual lusts and delights; [[3:3|living in malice and envy|in malitia et invidia agentes]], that is, working maliciously and enviously; [[3:3|hateful|odibiles]] to God and the Saints as regards the being of guilt [that is, insofar as they were in the state of sin]: according to that of Wisdom, [[Wis 14:9|to God the wicked and his wickedness are hateful alike|Odio sunt Deo impii et impietas ejus]]; and in the Psalm, [[Ps 5:7|Thou hatest all the workers of iniquity|Odisti omnes qui operantur iniquitatem]]; [[3:3|hating one another|odientes invicem]].

paras.t: Quum autem benignitas et humanitas apparuit Salvatoris nostri Dei: id est, hoc tempore gratiæ, quando advenit tempus plenitudo in qua statuit Deus succurrere mundo, sicut locutus est per os sanctorum qui a sæculo sunt Prophetarum ejus, apparuit mundo per Christi visibilem ac corporalem præsentiam, vel posterioribus, scilicet nobis, per fidem (de quibus dictum est: Beati qui non viderunt et crediderunt), benignitas, id est clementia, et humanitas a Verbo assumpta, Salvatoris nostri Dei, id est Christi, qui est Deus et salvator noster. Hæc apparuerunt visibiliter, Christo in terris cum hominibus conversante, quando circuivit benefaciendo et sanando omnes oppressos a diabolo.
paras.en: [[3:4|But when the goodness and kindness of God our Saviour appeared|Quum autem benignitas et humanitas apparuit Salvatoris nostri Dei]]: that is, in this time of grace, when the fulness of time came[[Gal 4:4||]] in which God determined to succour the world, [[Luke 1:70|As he spoke by the mouth of his holy prophets, who are from the beginning|sicut locutus est per os sanctorum qui a sæculo sunt Prophetarum ejus]], there appeared to the world through Christ's visible and bodily presence, or to those after, namely to us, through faith (of whom it is said: [[John 20:29|blessed are they that have not seen and have believed|Beati qui non viderunt et crediderunt]]), [[3:4|the goodness|benignitas, id est]] clemency, [[3:4|and kindness|et humanitas]] [*humanitas*, which the Douay-Rheims renders "kindness", is here taken as the humanity] assumed by the Word, [[3:4|of God our Saviour|Salvatoris nostri Dei, id est]] Christ, who is God and our Saviour. These appeared visibly when Christ was [[Bar 3:38|upon earth, and conversed with men|in terris cum hominibus conversante]], when he [[Acts 10:38|went about doing good and healing all that were oppressed by the devil|circuivit benefaciendo et sanando omnes oppressos a diabolo]].

paras.t: Non ex operibus justitiæ quæ fecimus nos, id est non propter merita nostra, quæ nulla fuerunt, quia prædictis eramus peccatis obnoxii, sed secundum suam misericordiam salvos nos fecit a potestate diaboli et reatu æterni tormenti, merito suæ conversationis et passionis, per lavacrum regenerationis, id est per Baptismum, qui est lotio qua ex aqua et Spiritu Sancto renascimur, et renovationis Spiritus Sancti, id est per interiorem lotionem seu infusionem gratiæ Spiritus Sancti, per quam anima spiritualiter renovatur, juxta illud: Renovamini spiritu mentis vestræ; et, Renovabitur ut aquilæ juventus tua. Quæ etiam lotio interior non solum confertur in Baptismo, sed et in sacramento Pœnitentiæ et ceteris sacramentis. Hæc ideo dicit Apostolus, quoniam licet Christus nos in cruce redemit sufficienter, oportet tamen ut meritum suæ passionis nobis per sacramenta applicetur, et primo per Baptismum, qui est janua sacramentorum.
paras.en: [[3:5|Not by the works of justice which we have done|Non ex operibus justitiæ quæ fecimus nos]], that is, not on account of our merits, which were none, since we were liable to the aforesaid sins, [[3:5|but according to his mercy, he saved us|sed secundum suam misericordiam salvos nos fecit]] from the power of the devil and the guilt of eternal torment, by the merit of his life and passion, [[3:5|by the laver of regeneration|per lavacrum regenerationis]], that is, by Baptism, which is the washing by which we are born again of water and the Holy Ghost[[John 3:5||]] [the margin gives John iii, 3; the words are those of John 3:5], [[3:5|and renovation of the Holy Ghost|et renovationis Spiritus Sancti]], that is, by the inward washing or infusion of the grace of the Holy Ghost, by which the soul is spiritually renewed, according to that: [[Eph 4:23|be renewed in spirit of your mind|Renovamini spiritu mentis vestræ]]; and: [[Ps 102:5|thy youth shall be renewed like the eagle's|Renovabitur ut aquilæ juventus tua]]. And this inward washing is conferred not only in Baptism, but also in the sacrament of Penance and the other sacraments. The Apostle says this because, although Christ redeemed us sufficiently on the cross, yet the merit of his passion must be applied to us through the sacraments, and first through Baptism, which is the gate of the sacraments.

paras.t: Quem Spiritum Sanctum, id est cujus dona et gratiam, effudit Deus Pater in nos abunde, id est clementer et copiose in Baptismo et postea, per Jesum Christum Salvatorem nostrum, id est merito Christi, de cujus plenitudine omnes accepimus, per quem omnia dona gratiæ derivantur ad nos; ut justificati, id est a nostris injustitiis et peccatis abluti, gratia ipsius, id est merito Christi, et per infusionem gratiæ suæ, heredes simus Dei, coheredesque Christi, id est filii adoptivi, secundum spem vitæ æternæ, id est vitam æternam sperando; vel, Heredes simus vitæ æternæ secundum spem, id est jam in spe, adepturi eam aliquando in re.
paras.en: [[3:6|Whom|Quem Spiritum]] the Holy Ghost, that is, whose gifts and grace, God the Father [[3:6|hath poured forth|effudit]] [[3:6|upon us abundantly|in nos abunde]], that is, mercifully and copiously, in Baptism and afterwards, [[3:6|through Jesus Christ our Saviour|per Jesum Christum Salvatorem nostrum]], that is, by the merit of Christ, [[John 1:16|of his fulness we all have received|de cujus plenitudine omnes accepimus]], through whom all the gifts of grace flow down to us; [[3:7|That, being justified|ut justificati]], that is, washed from our injustices and sins, [[3:7|by his grace|gratia ipsius]], that is, by the merit of Christ and by the infusion of his grace, [[3:7|we may be heirs|heredes simus Dei]] [[Rom 8:17|of God and joint heirs with Christ|coheredesque Christi]], that is, adoptive sons, [[3:7|according to hope of life everlasting|secundum spem vitæ æternæ]], that is, by hoping for eternal life; or: We may be heirs of eternal life according to hope, that is, already in hope, being one day to obtain it in reality.

paras.t: Fidelis sermo est quem dixi, atque dicturus sum. Et de his jam dictis, videlicet de gratia et beneficiis Christi, volo te confirmare, id est, volo ut in cognitione et dilectione istorum confirmeris a me, et gregem tibi commissum prædicando confirmes, ut curent bonis operibus præesse, id est exemplariter se habere, vel in virtutibus præcedere, vel non solum dignitate et nomine, sed vita et moribus præesse subjectis, qui credunt Deo, id est fideles, præsertim in prælationibus constituti. Hæc documenta sunt bona, id est vera in se, et utilia hominibus.
paras.en: [[3:8|It is a faithful saying|Fidelis sermo est]], which I have spoken and am about to speak. [[3:8|And these things|Et de his]] now said, namely of the grace and benefits of Christ, [[3:8|I will have thee affirm constantly|volo te confirmare]], that is, I will that thou be confirmed by me in the knowledge and love of them, and that by preaching thou confirm the flock committed to thee [the Latin *confirmare* allows both senses, "to be confirmed" and "to confirm"]; that [[3:8|may be careful to excel in good works|ut curent bonis operibus præesse]] [*præesse*, "to be over", "to go before"; the Douay-Rheims renders it "excel"], that is, bear themselves as an example, or go before others in virtues, or be over their subjects not only in dignity and name but in life and conduct, [[3:8|they who believe in God|qui credunt Deo]], that is, the faithful, especially those set in prelacies. [[3:8|These things are good|Hæc documenta sunt bona]], these teachings, that is, true in themselves, [[3:8|and profitable unto men|et utilia hominibus]].

paras.t: Stultas autem, id est superfluas et infructuosas, quæstiones, et genealogias, id est generationum enumerationes a Judæis confictas, quæ non habentur in Scriptura canonica: sicut quod Adam habuit duas uxores, de quarum qualibet plurimos generavit; et contentiones de observatione legalium tempore novi Testamenti, et pugnas legis, id est verbosas litigationes, quæ oriuntur ex locis Scripturarum quæ sibi contraria videntur, devita. Sunt enim inutiles et vanæ.
paras.en: But [[3:9|foolish|Stultas autem]], that is, superfluous and fruitless, [[3:9|questions and genealogies|quæstiones, et genealogias]], that is, enumerations of generations made up by the Jews, which are not found in canonical Scripture[[1 Tim 1:4||]]: as that Adam had two wives, of each of whom he begot very many; [[3:9|and contentions|et contentiones]] about the observance of the legal ceremonies in the time of the New Testament, [[3:9|and strivings about the law|et pugnas legis]], that is, wordy disputes, which arise from places of Scripture that seem contrary to one another, [[3:9|avoid|devita]]. [[3:9|For they are unprofitable and vain|Sunt enim inutiles et vanæ]].

paras.t: Hæreticum hominem post unam et secundam correptionem, id est, quum bis correptus fuerit, semel in privato, deinde in publico, et emendari noluerit, […]: sciens quod subvertitur, id est incorrigibiliter errans et perditus, est, qui hujusmodi est, et delinquit, id est peccat, quum sit proprio judicio condemnatus, id est propria electione et determinatione causam damnationis assumens, quoniam falsitatem pertinaciter servat, veritatem repellens.
paras.en: [[3:10|A man that is a heretic|Hæreticum hominem]] [[3:10|after the first and second admonition|post unam et secundam correptionem]], that is, when he has been rebuked twice, once in private[[Matt 18:15||]], then in public[[Matt 18:17||]], and will not amend, […] [a word or two are lost here, probably the end of the verse, *devita*, "avoid"]: [[3:11|Knowing that|sciens quod]] [[3:11|he that is such an one|qui hujusmodi est]] [[3:11|is subverted|subvertitur]], that is, goes astray incorrigibly and is lost, [[3:11|and sinneth|et delinquit]], that is, commits sin, being [[3:11|condemned by his own judgment|proprio judicio condemnatus]], that is, by his own choice and determination taking upon himself the cause of his damnation, since he obstinately holds to falsehood, rejecting the truth.

paras.t: Quum misero ad te Artemam aut Tychicum, ut unus eorum pro te Cretensibus præsit, ne populus Christi sit sicut oves sine pastore, festina ad me venire Nicopolim. Ibi enim statui, id est, in illa urbe proposui, hiemare.
paras.en: [[3:12|When I shall send to thee Artemas or Tychicus|Quum misero ad te Artemam aut Tychicum]], so that one of them may be over the Cretans in thy place, lest the people of Christ be as sheep without a shepherd, [[3:12|make haste to come unto me to Nicopolis|festina ad me venire Nicopolim]]. [[3:12|For there I have determined|Ibi enim statui]], that is, I have purposed in that city, [[3:12|to winter|hiemare]].

paras.t: Zenam legisperitum, qui hujus professionis erat in synagoga, et Apollo, qui non erat imperitior illo, quamvis non vocetur legisperitus, quoniam hujus professionis non fuit; fuit autem in Scripturis potens; sollicite præmitte ad me, sic tamen ut nihil de victualibus et necessariis illis desit in via.
paras.en: [[3:13|Zenas the lawyer|Zenam legisperitum]], who was of that profession in the synagogue, [[3:13|and Apollo|et Apollo]], who was not less learned than he, though he is not called a lawyer, since he was not of that profession; but he was [[Acts 18:24|mighty in the scriptures|in Scripturis potens]]: [[3:13|with care|sollicite]] [[3:13|Send forward|præmitte]] to me, yet so [[3:13|that nothing|ut nihil]] of food and necessaries [[3:13|be wanting to them|illis desit]] on the way.

paras.t: Discant autem, id est, per operationem scire studeant, et nostri, id est Christiani inter Cretenses, bonis operibus præesse sibi ipsis, id est bene operando se ipsos gubernare, ad usus necessarios, id est ad hoc ut prædicatoribus Evangelii necessaria præbeant, ut non sint infructuosi, id est sine merito, eo quod non dent carnalia iis a quibus recipiunt spiritualia. Hoc dicit Apostolus, ut ostendat Tito unde possit Zenæ et Apollo de necessariis providere. Tanquam dicat: A subditis tuis, quibus et illi prædicaverunt, recipere debes.
paras.en: And let them [[3:14|learn|Discant autem]], that is, let them study to know it by doing, [[3:14|our men also|et nostri]], that is, the Christians among the Cretans, [[3:14|to excel in good works|bonis operibus præesse]] for themselves, that is, to govern themselves by working well, [[3:14|for necessary uses|ad usus necessarios]], that is, so that they furnish the preachers of the Gospel with what they need, [[3:14|that they be not unfruitful|ut non sint infructuosi]], that is, without merit, because they do not give carnal things to those from whom they receive spiritual things[[1 Cor 9:11||]]. The Apostle says this to show Titus whence he can provide Zenas and Apollo with necessaries; as if he said: Thou oughtest to receive them from thy subjects, to whom these also have preached.

paras.t: Salutant te qui mecum sunt omnes fideles, quos gratia brevitatis nominatim non exprimo. Saluta eos qui nos amant in fide, id est, eo quod fideles sumus; vel, In fide, id est fideli affectu, non ficte. Gratia Dei sit semper cum omnibus vobis, id est tecum et cum adjutoribus ac subditis tuis: qui omnes incessabiliter indigetis gratia Creatoris, qui est super omnia Deus sublimis et benedictus. Amen.
paras.en: [[3:15|All that are with me salute thee|Salutant te qui mecum sunt omnes]], all the faithful, whom for brevity's sake I do not name. [[3:15|Salute them that love us in the faith|Saluta eos qui nos amant in fide]], that is, because we are faithful; or, [[3:15|in the faith|In fide, id est]] with faithful affection, not feignedly. [[3:15|The grace of God|Gratia Dei]] be always [[3:15|with you all|cum omnibus vobis]], that is, with thee and with thy helpers and subjects: who all unceasingly stand in need of the grace of the Creator, who is God over all, exalted and blessed. [[3:15|Amen|Amen]].
